You are the implementer for unit t6-jev-doc-park (closing docs unit of the "Jev in ringer" run), running as a ringer worker with no conversation history; everything you need is in this spec.

WORKSPACE AND BOUNDARY
- Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the ringer repo, detached at the current commit of branch jev-ringer; edit files here directly and run every command from here.
- Never read from, edit, or run commands inside /home/jjrdar/repos/ringer (the main checkout).
- Leave every change uncommitted: never run `git commit`, `git stash`, `git reset`, `git checkout`, or anything else that moves HEAD; the check stages and exports your diff.
- Never create or modify a path outside the ownership list below.
- Never set or export TYPESAFE_API_KEY and never make a network call.
- Never use the em dash character (Unicode U+2014); use a plain "-".

OWNERSHIP LIST (the only paths you may create or modify)
- docs/JEV.md
- docs/handoffs/2026-09-23.t6-jev-doc-park.resume.md

THE TASK
In docs/JEV.md, replace the whole `## FAIL flag gate` section (from the line `## FAIL flag gate` up to, but not including, the line `## task_type`) with EXACTLY the text between the markers below, byte for byte, including the trailing blank line before `## task_type`.
Do not change any other byte of the file.

=====BEGIN REPLACEMENT (do not include this marker line)=====
## FAIL flag gate

The FAIL flag is parked as of 2026-09-23, and `fail_flag = true` has no effect because the flag was never built.
The offline replay ran once on 2026-09-23 with contract `fail_flag-v1` over the 47 logged FAIL pairs and missed the bar: it flagged 0 of the 11 labeled check_bug tasks and 0 tasks overall, with a highest `check` probability of 0.78 against the 0.9 cutoff.
The replay script `scripts/jev_fail_replay.py` still sends each logged task's first FAIL to Jev with the same fields and caps a live flag would use, writes `results.jsonl`, `summary.json`, and `review.csv` into its `--out` directory, and is safe to rerun, because finished pairs are skipped.
The bar it scores is unchanged: `bar_met: true` needs at least 9 of the 11 labeled check_bug tasks flagged, and hand-judged wrong flags in `review.csv` plus `false_flags` must total at most 20% of `flags_total`.
The plan's one allowed rewording (`fail_flag-v2`) was not spent, because the declared fields, not the wording, are the likely limit; the handoff `docs/handoffs/2026-09-23.jev-fail-flag-parked.md` records the evidence and the follow-up candidates.
=====END REPLACEMENT (do not include this marker line)=====

Then write your resume pointer at docs/handoffs/2026-09-23.t6-jev-doc-park.resume.md with these heading lines, verbatim and in this order, each followed by its content, one full sentence per line:

(the unit name, "closing docs unit of the jev-ringer loop-drive run, plan docs/plans/2026-09-23.jev-ringer-plan.md", and "tracker issue: none")

(one or two sentences: the changes are uncommitted in a ringer worktree of branch jev-ringer, and that you verified the section matches the replacement text exactly)
## Next step
(the single next action: the orchestrator validates /home/jjrdar/ringer-work/jev-ringer/patches/t6-jev-doc-park.patch and commits it on jev-ringer)
## Recent artifacts
(one "- " bullet each: docs/handoffs/2026-09-23.jev-fail-flag-parked.md, docs/JEV.md, docs/handoffs/2026-09-23.t6-jev-doc-park.resume.md)

WHAT THE CHECK VERIFIES
- docs/JEV.md's `## FAIL flag gate` section equals the replacement text byte for byte, and every other byte of the file equals the committed version.
- HEAD is unchanged, `git add -A` stages only the two ownership paths, and both are present.
- No added line contains the em dash character.
- The resume pointer exists with the four `## ` headings in order and at least one artifact bullet.
tasks.check:
set -u
fail() { printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$*"; exit 1; }
KEY=t6-jev-doc-park
MAIN=/home/jjrdar/repos/ringer
OUT=/home/jjrdar/ringer-work/jev-ringer/patches
PATCH="$OUT/$KEY.patch"
RESUME="docs/handoffs/2026-09-23.$KEY.resume.md"
top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || fail "cwd $PWD is not inside a git worktree"
[ "$top" = "$PWD" ] || fail "check cwd $PWD is not the worktree root ($top)"
[ "$PWD" != "$MAIN" ] || fail "check is running in the main checkout"
base=$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse refs/heads/jev-ringer) || fail "cannot read branch jev-ringer"
[ "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$base" ] || fail "worktree HEAD is not the jev-ringer tip: something moved HEAD"
python3 - <<'PY' || fail "docs/JEV.md does not match the expected result (details above)"
import subprocess, sys, difflib
NEW = "## FAIL flag gate\n\nThe FAIL flag is parked as of 2026-09-23, and `fail_flag = true` has no effect because the flag was never built.\nThe offline replay ran once on 2026-09-23 with contract `fail_flag-v1` over the 47 logged FAIL pairs and missed the bar: it flagged 0 of the 11 labeled check_bug tasks and 0 tasks overall, with a highest `check` probability of 0.78 against the 0.9 cutoff.\nThe replay script `scripts/jev_fail_replay.py` still sends each logged task's first FAIL to Jev with the same fields and caps a live flag would use, writes `results.jsonl`, `summary.json`, and `review.csv` into its `--out` directory, and is safe to rerun, because finished pairs are skipped.\nThe bar it scores is unchanged: `bar_met: true` needs at least 9 of the 11 labeled check_bug tasks flagged, and hand-judged wrong flags in `review.csv` plus `false_flags` must total at most 20% of `flags_total`.\nThe plan's one allowed rewording (`fail_flag-v2`) was not spent, because the declared fields, not the wording, are the likely limit; the handoff `docs/handoffs/2026-09-23.jev-fail-flag-parked.md` records the evidence and the follow-up candidates.\n"
old = subprocess.run(["git", "show", "HEAD:docs/JEV.md"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
have = open("docs/JEV.md", encoding="utf-8").read()
a = old.index("## FAIL flag gate\n"); b = old.index("## task_type\n")
want = old[:a] + NEW + old[b:]
if have == old:
    print("docs/JEV.md is unchanged from HEAD; the FAIL flag gate section was not rewritten"); sys.exit(1)
if have != want:
    print("docs/JEV.md differs from the expected file; first differences:")
    print("\n".join(list(difflib.unified_diff(want.splitlines(), have.splitlines(), "expected", "docs/JEV.md", lineterm="", n=1))[:40])); sys.exit(1)
PY
git add -A || fail "git add failed"
stray=$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep -vxF -e docs/JEV.md -e "$RESUME")
[ -z "$stray" ] || fail "scope violation: $(printf '%s ' $stray)"
for f in docs/JEV.md "$RESUME"; do git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qxF "$f" || fail "required path $f not staged"; done
EM=$(printf '\342\200\224')
em=$(git diff --cached -U0 --no-color | grep '^+' | grep -v '^+++ ' | grep -F "$EM" | head -n 3)
[ -z "$em" ] || fail "em dash in added lines: $em"
python3 - "$RESUME" <<'PY' || fail "resume pointer $RESUME lacks the required headings (details above)"
import sys
lines = [l.rstrip() for l in open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines()]
if not lines or not lines[0].startswith("# Resume pointer:"): sys.exit("first line must start with '# Resume pointer:'")
want = ["## Unit", "## State", "## Next step", "## Recent artifacts"]
missing = [h for h in want if h not in lines]
if missing: sys.exit(f"missing heading(s): {missing}")
idx = [lines.index(h) for h in want]
if idx != sorted(idx): sys.exit("headings out of order")
if not any(l.startswith("- ") for l in lines[idx[-1] + 1:]): sys.exit("## Recent artifacts has no bullet")
PY
mkdir -p "$OUT" && git diff --cached --binary > "$PATCH" || fail "could not write $PATCH"
[ -s "$PATCH" ] || fail "exported patch is empty"
echo "OK: $KEY - FAIL flag gate section rewritten exactly, rest of docs/JEV.md byte-identical, scope clean, patch $PATCH"
